common_instruction: This is a response-only exercise. Use the supplied scenario and snippets; propose or review the requested work without claiming files were changed, commands ran, or external systems were inspected. State material verification limits. Equivalent solutions that satisfy the stated contract are acceptable.

cases.name: two-diverging-copies-can-justify-one-rule-owner
cases.prompt: Two Python paths, checkout and renewal, must apply the same accepted eligibility rule: account age is at least 18 and identity is verified. Both initially copied that check. Renewal recently changed to checking only verified, producing a confirmed defect. There are exactly two copies. A review says extraction must wait for a third copy. Recommend a bounded fix that preserves the rule and prevents this divergence; no generic policy engine is needed.
expectations: Repairs renewal to the accepted two-condition eligibility rule.
Treats the shared business obligation and observed divergence as sufficient reason for a small common rule owner despite there being only two copies.
Covers both checkout and renewal callers and disqualifying combinations in focused checks.
Keeps unrelated caller-specific behavior outside the shared rule.
negative_expectations: Must not defer fixing the shared source of divergence solely to satisfy a rule-of-three threshold.
Must not introduce a generic policy engine, registry, or multi-layer class hierarchy for this one predicate.
cases.trap: Enforce an abstraction-count heuristic after duplication has already broken a shared business rule.

cases.name: similar-arithmetic-is-not-shared-domain-policy
cases.prompt: A Python package has two short functions with similar multiplication code. Invoice tax rounds money using the invoicing contract; sensor calibration preserves full floating-point precision using a device-specific scale. They have different owners and change independently. A proposal merges them into calculate(value, factor, round_result=False, mode=...) to reduce line duplication. Review the proposal and identify the smallest useful design direction.
expectations: Keeps the distinct domain rules independently understandable rather than merging them solely because the expressions look alike.
Explains that a shared stable mechanism could be extracted later if one actually exists, without treating all duplication as forbidden.
negative_expectations: Must not introduce mode flags that couple unrelated policies or change either numerical contract for reuse.
Must not justify abstraction solely with copy count or line count.
cases.trap: Confuse similar syntax with one shared business responsibility and hide different semantics behind configuration flags.
